## Design

### 2026-11-12: Nov 11: First Session on the 4-Bit Adder

**4h**

Nov 11: First Session on the 4-Bit Adder

This Project is a massive one for me. For it to be manageable, it should be divided into simpler steps. The first step in this project is designing a 1-bit adder and then expanding it to add 4 bits. At first, I tried to design it myself, but I quickly realized that this is no easy task. To help me along the way, I found this gem on YouTube: (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7a8hRhPL9bs&t=2s). This Channel has everything I need to understand the process of creating an adder from logic gates. I was mind-blown by how easy the process was! The adder works by splitting the addition process into two separate parts: one for (2^0) and another for (2^1). For (2^0), an AND gate is used, while for (2^1), an XOR gate is used. And this is the circuit.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/2d9c6e2265047c594a2eb85df17884729ee97822fe3502d7d4b93b6345f0900f.png)

After designing this 1-bit adder, it was time for the next stage: the 2-bit adder. However, a 2-bit adder requires three inputs instead of two because the previous addition may generate a carry bit. Again, I tried to figure it out on my own, but I failed horribly; I wasn't close at all. I opened YouTube again and got the general idea for the 2-bit adder, but I ended up with only three output slots instead of four (I later discovered that it needed only 3 XD). I don't know why, but it doesn't work as it is supposed to

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/1805fd300ab681e66368213ab4ef7eb1485b882dfbe7d804d6ff151a2a4a27b4.png)

I think my mistake was not taking the carry bit from the first addition into account. So, I decided to go the traditional route and design an addition circuit with three inputs: A, B, and C (carry-in). And here is my adder design! (This is the same design as the guide Video I followed)

I redesigned the 2-bit adder, and here it is! After the changes, I finally had a fully working 2-bit adder.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/dbab73f08f804c578020d5ef5a77af5ba25fcd26e63d96f507632a3ec0bc727c.png)

I then noticed that the red lines weren't connected to anything, meaning the gates connected to them served no purpose. So, I refined the design even further to create the final-final version.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/57613c7997e4ec777c1992670d9cd5ee5a84d6ea01267c861661b7fd87ba4937.png)

Now, building 3-bit and 4-bit adders should simply be a matter of repeating the same process!

Total Time Spent: 4 hours.

Most of it was spent fixing mistakes and rewatching the YouTube guide, but it was worth it for me :)

**Tl;dr:** The adder circuit was designed from Gates.

### 2026-11-12: **12 Nov: Designing the Logic Gates**

**7h**

**12 Nov: Designing the Logic Gates**

I only need to design three logic gates for this project: AND, OR, &XOR. And to do that, of course, I watched a YouTube tutorial,

**AND Gate:**

The AND gate was pretty easy to design. It consists of two transistors connected in series, meaning the circuit won't turn on unless both transistors are powered. I'm not entirely sure if there are any additional resistors or components I should add, but for now, I think it's solid. (spoilers: It wasn't solid at all)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/429f346875ce626b1f7f7ae00d2ae71f45f91483af1b79f56c29a318dba0b574.png)

**OR Gate:**

Next was the OR gate. It follows a similar concept, but this time the transistors are connected in parallel, with both paths leading to the same output. (Tbh, I'm not even sure if I'll need the OR gate for now. If I shorted both wires to the same output, wouldn't this serve the same purpose?)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/383778897f173c3dea30852315ddd7b008159bd32a9d95044eb2dbe0dcb883cf.png)

I found the answer to this question near the end of this session. Since if one input is low, current will flow back to the other input, making the output a float instead of a High or Low. However, this isn't much of an issue, since adding a couple of diodes will fix this problem, and I later implemented this solution.

**XOR Gate:**

Now for the final gate: the XOR. This one is a little more interesting because it uses both AND and OR logic. I didn't quite understand what it did, but I got it after reading that XOR = OR − AND.

The schematic connects both gates using another transistor. When the AND gate is active, current flows through that path and disables the switch, leaving the output LOW. Other than this It works similar to standered and and OR gates.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/7715482ce9560fda539a6430dd90550421a73d6ff7636968e3e106f55a0799be.png)

**1-Bit Adder  Circuit:**

And with that, all three gates are designed! Now it's time to build the 1-bit adder and then expand it into the full adder module.

I started by designing the adder for Bit_1, using the same model I created in the previous session.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/f8b553ce58b0687735335d2133ea09bbf327cdb9e34cc2c4603f8597f0ab3207.png)

I thought to myself that I should check the circuits I built before assembling the adders together. And, after a quick one-minute search, I discovered that I needed a 2kΩ resistor for each input. I also discovered a ton of problems with my design. For example, BIT_1_Out was accidentally shorted to the other two transistors, and the output needed a pull-down resistor.

(Future me here: Those designs lacked any Type of resistor, like on the input, a pull-down resistor to ground to keep from acting like a noise picker. and so on. Figuring all this out and the exact resistance I should use was a headache; each website has its own design, and each design has a totally different resistance, and some designs have LEDs. This was really bad)

** Troubleshooting **

I searched online again for other circuit designs, but I couldn't find anything simple enough to follow.

So, I decided to try the circuits first on an electronic circuit simulator. Thank God I did! It turned out that the AND gate wasn't working at all.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/70e10b80220b2ba14ebd679d0ac02dde607ccd71e3cd79f8cf4ff74112f8b151.png)

 I changed the resistor values to 22kΩ, and suddenly, it worked like magic! So I did the same to all the circuits

Next, I tried building the XOR gate using the same setup, but it didn't work at first either. I spent hours trying to figure out what was wrong, only to discover that the problem was simply the orientation of one of the transistors. Apparently, on this site (Falstad.com) you can change the type of transistor by using the scroll wheel, so I assume that this is what happened; before figuring this out, I even tried designing the circuit without any crossing wires, and this made the wires short, creating a weak signal. I had major problems with the resistance of each part of the circuit; it was just hell.

### 2026-11-13: Before starting to work on the PCB, I decided to build the full adder on a circuit simulator to check if there are any issues. I successfully emulated the circuit. At first, the circuit didn't work ca

**8h**

Before starting to work on the PCB, I decided to build the full adder on a circuit simulator to check if there are any issues. I successfully emulated the circuit. At first, the circuit didn't work cause I didn't wire it correctly; after reworking the circuit, everything now works as it should. Also, there was a problem with reading the output from bit 2, as it was set to LOW when It should be HIGH; the wire had current too. I fixed this problem by decreasing the threshold to 2 instead of 2.5.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/5ff0638daf3092282c1c7006918e3bf4d02b1d4a755a4b4ae63847754a14e8ab.png)

I continued building the full adder, but as seen in the image, it doesn't work. It was just a problem with connecting the AND gates of the carry bit. Now it's fixed, and the adder works fine. But there is an issue with the voltage drops due to the wire length in the simulator; I will ignore this issue, as in real circuits the wires will be much shorter

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/26d200403a076b0ed265c8c0539761734cc87d877b90bf5c86e17bd13ed63bb4.png)
